page: Microsoft Azure E8d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector instructions, cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, and virtualization extensions.

This server is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a 307 GB local solid-state drive (SSD), which provides fast local scratch space. No GPU accelerators are present in this configuration.

Benchmark data places the E8d_v5 in the average performance tier across most compute and memory metrics. The single-core stress-ng score is 1898.48, and the multi-core score is 7760.02. Memory bandwidth tests show 415.87 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 56.69 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations via Passmark score 4029.97, and Redis SET operations reach 7.75 million operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium-sized LLM inference (7B model) show weaker relative performance, with the 7B model achieving 7.71 tokens per second for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E8d_v5 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require extreme CPU scaling. The inclusion of local SSD storage reduces the need for external storage attachments for temporary data. This virtual machine is suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, data buffering, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
